metadata.title: Battlefield Terrain Database -- Key Locations, Roads, and Features
sources: Desjardin, Thomas A. -- The Battlefield at Gettysburg (Map), The Gettysburg Foundation, 2011
Gottfried, Bradley M. -- The Maps of Gettysburg (Savas Beatie, 2013)
Laino, Phillip -- Gettysburg Campaign Atlas (Gettysburg Publishing, 2014)

key_locations.name: Cemetery Hill
key_locations.significance: Union army's central anchor. XI Corps and artillery reserve. Osborn's massed guns dominated the battlefield. Hays and Avery attacked here July 2 evening.

key_locations.name: Culp's Hill
key_locations.significance: Union right flank anchor. XII Corps held against Johnson's division. Greene's lone stand July 2 night. Seven hours of fighting July 3 morning.

key_locations.name: Little Round Top
key_locations.significance: Key terrain on Union left. Vincent's brigade arrived just in time July 2. 20th Maine held the extreme left. O'Rorke charged without orders. Hazlett dragged guns up the slope.

key_locations.name: Big Round Top
key_locations.significance: Highest terrain on the battlefield. Fisher's brigade occupied it July 2 evening. Crawford's charge passed near its base.

key_locations.name: Devil's Den
key_locations.significance: Rocky terrain south of Little Round Top. Ward's brigade and Smith's battery. Texas Brigade assault. Famous sharpshooter position.

key_locations.name: The Wheatfield
key_locations.significance: John Rose's wheatfield. Scene of six Confederate and nine Union brigade engagements July 2. Changed hands multiple times. Nearly 6,000 casualties.

key_locations.name: Peach Orchard
key_locations.significance: Sickles's unauthorized salient. Barksdale's charge destroyed the position. Graham captured here.

key_locations.name: Trostle Farm
key_locations.significance: Bigelow's battery fought withdrawal here. Famous cannon shot through the barn. McGilvery built his Plum Run Line nearby.

key_locations.name: The Angle (High Water Mark)
key_locations.significance: The furthest Confederate penetration of the battle. Armistead crossed the stone wall here. Cushing's battery was at this spot. Copse of trees marks the point today.

key_locations.name: Seminary Ridge (central)
key_locations.significance: Confederate main line July 2-3. 170 Confederate guns along this ridge for the July 3 cannonade. Alexander directed from here.

key_locations.name: Cemetery Ridge (central)
key_locations.significance: Union main defensive line July 2-3. II Corps position. The Army of the Potomac's defensive backbone.

key_locations.name: McPherson's Ridge
key_locations.significance: First major defensive position July 1. Buford's dismounted cavalry then Reynolds's I Corps. Iron Brigade charged into Herbst Woods from this ridge.

key_locations.name: Herbst Woods (McPherson's Woods)
key_locations.significance: Iron Brigade charged into these woods July 1 morning. Reynolds killed at eastern edge. Archer's Confederate brigade broken and Archer captured.

key_locations.name: Oak Ridge
key_locations.significance: Baxter's ambush destroyed Iverson's brigade here. Paul's brigade fought here with four commanders wounded in succession. Mass grave of Iverson's men visible today.

key_locations.name: Oak Hill
key_locations.significance: Confederate artillery on Oak Hill provided flanking fire on Union I Corps. Rodes's division attacked from here.

key_locations.name: Barlow's Knoll
key_locations.significance: XI Corps right flank. Barlow wounded here. Gordon's flank attack struck this position. Wilkeson's battery destroyed here.

key_locations.name: Railroad Cut (western)
key_locations.significance: Davis's brigade trapped here by 6th Wisconsin's charge July 1. Mass captures. Gettysburg Animated YouTube vignette subject.

key_locations.name: Herr Ridge
key_locations.significance: Pegram's Confederate artillery opened fire from here July 1 morning. Heth's division deployed across this ridge before advancing.

key_locations.name: Bliss Farm
key_locations.significance: Contested skirmish position between Seminary and Cemetery ridges July 2-3. Changed hands nine times. Finally burned July 3.

key_locations.name: Benner's Hill
key_locations.significance: Latimer's Confederate battalion placed here July 2. Destroyed by Union counterbattery fire. Latimer (age 19) mortally wounded.

key_locations.name: East Cavalry Field
key_locations.significance: Stuart vs Gregg/Custer July 3. Stuart attempted to reach Union rear during Pickett's Charge. Custer's charge stopped him. Hampton wounded.

key_locations.name: Lutheran Theological Seminary
key_locations.significance: Cupola used by both sides for observation. Perrin's Confederate brigade drove through Seminary grounds July 1. Seminary Ridge named for this building.

key_locations.name: Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse
key_locations.significance: Union headquarters area. Howard established headquarters here July 1. Evergreen Cemetery on the hill.

key_locations.name: Codori Farm
key_locations.significance: Near the advance Confederate skirmish positions July 3. Confederate attacking line passed through this farm during Pickett's Charge.

key_locations.name: Spangler's Spring
key_locations.significance: XII Corps area between Culp's Hill and Cemetery Hill. Famous disputed truce during the night of July 2 where Union and Confederate soldiers reportedly shared water.

key_locations.name: Plum Run (valley)
key_locations.significance: Valley between the Round Tops and Cemetery Ridge. 1st Minnesota charged toward this creek to stop Wilcox. McGilvery's Plum Run Line established here.

key_locations.name: Rose Woods
key_locations.significance: Fighting between Peach Orchard and Wheatfield. DeTrobriand's and Kershaw's brigades fought here. Stone wall along northern edge.

key_locations.name: Power's Hill
key_locations.significance: XII Corps reserve position. Artillery on crest. Slocum's headquarters area.

key_locations.name: Gulp's Hill saddle
key_locations.significance: Low ground between Culp's Hill and Cemetery Hill. Key terrain in XII Corps defensive line.

key_locations.name: Triangular Field
key_locations.significance: Rocky field below Devil's Den. Ward's brigade fought here. Texas Brigade assault through this terrain.

roads.name: Chambersburg Pike (US Route 30)
roads.significance: Main Confederate approach route. Heth's division advanced east on this road July 1. Iron Brigade fought near this road.

roads.name: Emmitsburg Road
roads.significance: Sickles advanced to this road July 2 creating his salient. Humphreys's division fought along it. Main Union approach route.

roads.name: Taneytown Road
roads.significance: Union supply and reinforcement route. Meade's headquarters on this road.

roads.name: Baltimore Pike
roads.significance: Union army's main line of communication and supply. XII Corps approached on this road.

roads.name: York Road
roads.significance: Early's Confederate division approached on this road July 1. Extra Billy Smith guarded the flank here.

roads.name: Carlisle Road
roads.significance: Rodes's Confederate division approached on this road, arriving at Oak Hill.

roads.name: Hagerstown Road
roads.significance: Confederate retreat route July 4-5. Anderson's division on this road.

roads.name: Mummasburg Road
roads.significance: Connects to Oak Ridge area. Used by Rodes for positioning.

structures.name: Meade's Headquarters (Leister House)
structures.significance: Army of Potomac headquarters July 2-3. Near miss from Confederate artillery July 3 cannonade.

structures.name: Lee's Headquarters
structures.significance: Near the Chambersburg Pike on Seminary Ridge.

structures.name: Trostle Farm barn
structures.significance: Bigelow's withdrawal. Famous cannonball hole in barn wall still visible today.

structures.name: Rose Farm
structures.significance: At center of the Wheatfield fighting. Rose's stone wall a key defensive feature.

structures.name: Codori Farm
structures.significance: On the open ground traversed by Pickett's charge.

structures.name: Brian Farm (Bryan Farm)
structures.significance: Adjacent to The Angle. Stood amid the fighting during Pickett's Charge.

structures.name: Lutheran Theological Seminary
structures.significance: Cupola used for observation. Perrin's charge broke through Seminary grounds July 1.

structures.name: Gettysburg railroad depot
structures.significance: Gettysburg & Harrisburg Railroad terminus. Hall's battery near this area July 1.

terrain_features.name: Stone walls (Cemetery Ridge)
terrain_features.significance: Key defensive feature. The wall at The Angle was the focal point of Pickett's Charge. Webb's and Cushing's positions.

terrain_features.name: Copse of Trees
terrain_features.significance: Visual reference point used by Confederate attackers during Pickett's Charge. Still standing today.

terrain_features.name: Gettysburg & Harrisburg Railroad Cut
terrain_features.significance: Davis's brigade trapped here. 6th Wisconsin's famous charge. Unfinished cut too deep to escape quickly.

terrain_features.name: Willoughby Run
terrain_features.significance: Small stream at base of McPherson's Ridge. Iron Brigade crossed this charging into Herbst Woods.
